# Narration Guide

<!-- Generated by `npm run guide` from scenes.json. Edit the text in scenes.json, then run it again. -->

13 scenes, 319 words, about 123 s of speech, 195 s planned on screen. The contest limit is 180 s; this project warns above 175 s.

## How to change the words and record your own voice

1. Edit `narration` for a scene in `demo/scenes.json`. Spell hard words the way they sound ("I D" for ID).
2. Record that scene alone, 44.1 or 48 kHz, one take per file. Keep a half second of quiet at each end.
3. Save it as `demo/public/audio/<scene-id>.wav` (`.mp3`, `.m4a` and `.aac` also work). Use the id in the table below.
   Your file replaces the machine voice for that scene. Delete your file to go back to the placeholder.
4. Run `npm run sync` (the studio and render scripts do this for you). The scene length follows your recording.
5. `npm run studio` to preview. `npm run render` for the full video, or `npm run render:scene -- s04-reveal out/s04.mp4` for one scene.

Machine-voice stand-ins: `npm run vo:placeholder` (uses the macOS `say` command, voice and speed set by
`PHANTOMTRACE_VO_VOICE` and `PHANTOMTRACE_VO_RATE`). Add `-- --all` to redo every scene after editing text.
The stand-in voice is only for timing. Replace it with your own before you submit.

## Pace and length

- Plan on about 2.6 words per second. A scene with 26 words needs about 10 seconds.
- Each scene lasts as long as your recording plus 0.6 s, or its video clip if that is longer.
- If the total is too long, cut words first, then trim clips with `trimStartSec` in `scenes.json`.

## Honest-claims check

Say only what the video shows. The Kiro scene says hooks "check" things before commits, because the hook
output was not captured (see `docs/KiroUsage.md`). If you add a claim, add its proof to the repo first.
